about.introduction_desc_2: Fun fact: I love to travel and draw architectural landscapes.
about.experience_desc_2: Content Designer and Conversation Designer @ Ally
about.toolbox_content_desc: I craft clear, intuitive and compassionate content design to guide the users and meet business goals.
about.toolbox_writing_desc: I build scalable content systems by aligning voice, tone and style to create a consistent and user-centered design.
about.toolbox_ux_desc: I collaborate with designers, product managers and developers to create a seamless user experience.
about.toolbox_product_desc: I bring designs to life by creating a seamless experience for users, ensuring to meet the user and the business needs.

dealer.description_hero: Digitized the Auto Dealer Financing platform for Ally Auto dealers to generate contract applications to lease their vehicles on behalf of their customers.
dealer.section_overview_desc: The existing process for dealers to submit contracts for funding was outdated and difficult to navigate, leading to confusion and frustration for dealers as they need to process all paperwork manually. The goal was to create a digitized platform that would streamline the contracting process and improve the overall user experience.
dealer.section_problem_desc: How might we redesign a platform to enable dealers to efficiently manage the contracting process online with no human in the loop?
dealer.section_metrics_desc_1: Digital all-in-one platform where dealers can handle their daily contract requests
dealer.section_metrics_desc_2: Increase in satisfaction scores from dealers regarding this transition
dealer.section_goals_desc_1: Enhance the leasing process through cohesive and intuitive user experience and content design.
dealer.section_goals_desc_2: Reduce confusion for dealers to efficiently navigate through the portal so they can focus on the application process.
dealer.section_collaboration: How I collaborated with product designers
dealer.section_scenario_desc: I led a working session to map out the scenarios to understand the user journey and identify potential pain points.
dealer.section_research_desc: I collaborated with researchers to conduct user interviews to understand the needs of the users. I then created a user flow to visualize the end-to-end process.
dealer.section_heuristic_desc: We conducted a heuristic evaluation to identify usability issues and areas for improvement in the existing platform.
dealer.section_wireframe_desc: I created wireframes to visualize the layout and structure of the new platform, focusing on improving usability and efficiency.
dealer.section_prototype_desc: I collaborated with the product designers to create a high-fidelity prototype that incorporated the feedback from user testing and heuristic evaluation.
dealer.section_impact_1: 81% of users reported satisfaction with the new web portal.
dealer.section_impact_2: 92% of users reported that the instructions were clear and easy to follow.
dealer.section_learning_1: Use of analytics and A/B testing
dealer.section_learning_2: Taking full ownership of an App design
dealer.section_learning_3: Manage a basic roadmap of features
assist.description_hero: Designed a compassionate chatbot to assist customers who need help understanding options for missed payments.
assist.section_overview_desc: Due to the impact of post-pandemic inflation, 34% of customers need help with either delaying their next few payments or changing the payment contract to reduce their monthly payment (Based on NLP data from Ally Customer Base).
assist.section_problem_desc_1: How might we effectively interact with customers who are experiencing financial hardship and are concerned they may miss payments in the next few months?
assist.section_problem_desc_3: Reduction in call and chat volumes handled by human associates in our Contact Center.
assist.section_problem_desc_4: Reduction in the number of customers going into collections for missing a payment.
assist.section_flow_desc: Based on the requirements and user research, I sketched the user flow to visualize the conversation design. This helped me identify key touchpoints and potential pain points in the user journey.
assist.section_convo_desc: I mapped the end-to-end user journey, including identifying user intents, possible scenarios and edge cases.
assist.section_testing_desc: The main goal was to understand the level of information users need before committing to the process and to learn if the information is clear to understand to the users.
assist.section_numbers_1: Users felt the information provided throughout the conversation was just right.
assist.section_numbers_2: Users felt certain complex financial terms around payments was unclear.
assist.section_numbers_3: On a scale of 1-5, the users felt the chat messages were educational & compassionate.
assist.section_approach_1_desc: I took the approach to use straightforward language to ensure that the information is easy to understand for users who might be stressed about their financial situations.
assist.section_feedback_legal_1: Direct language around payments might be too promissory to users
assist.section_feedback_legal_3: Example: can -> might be able to
assist.section_approach_2_desc: There were technical limitations and security concerns around pulling user data when they haven’t missed their payment, so I added an option to direct user to the internal payment assistance tool to see if they qualify.
assist.section_outcome_desc_1: 23% reduction in chat and call volumes
assist.section_outcome_desc_2: 18% less customers going into collections for missing a payment
assist.section_outcome_desc_3: Boosted customer’s confidence in discussing their situation with human associates (based on Ally Customer data and survey results from Q1 2025).
women.description_hero: Explored the differences of women with their finances to evaluate how financial institutions can better support their financial journey, while keeping all customers in mind.
women.section_overview_desc_1: Understanding and connecting with women as a financial ally is as important as ever. Women play an increasingly critical role in steering America’s money, from managing household budgets to maintaining multi-generational wealth.
women.section_overview_desc_2: Despite being such a critical segment to win, women broadly don’t feel as understood, valued or supported by their financial institutions compare to men. Women may have different needs from what their financial institutions traditionally provide.
women.section_overview_desc_3: The question is... are we doing what we can to recognize and support those unique needs?
women.section_problem_desc_2: Extensive gender analysis of Ally customer engagement and marketing data
women.section_problem_desc_3: 3rd party market research (KANTAR, Forrester, Mintel, JD Power) and government sponsored data (Census Bureau, FINRA, FRB)
women.section_problem_desc_4: In-depth interviews with 36 women, 4 men, and 4 non-binary individuals.
women.section_bigpicture_desc: A monumental transition of wealth is imminent. On average, women live about five years longer than men, likely gaining ownership of any assets that weren’t already under their control. As of 2020, women controlled about a third of investable household financial assets worth over $10 trillion, but women will soon take over much of the $30 trillion in wealth that baby boomers are expected to hold by 2030.
women.section_lead_desc: More women have controls over their life and financial decisions than ever before in the U.S. The effect of women’s longevity is already in play in real estate — single women own 58% of homes owned by unmarried Americans and account for about two-thirds of the head of households for ages 65 and older.
women.section_lead_desc_1: Of women are unmarried, with many having never been married
women.section_lead_desc_2: Of divorces over age 50 are initiated by women
women.section_lead_desc_3: Of women state they have primary or joint responsibility for household spending decisions
women.section_lead_desc_4: Of the senior leadership positions at top companies are held by women
women.section_barriers_desc: Despite the social and economic progress women have made over the past few decades, there are still significant barriers they face on their paths to financial equity. These financial disadvantages can have a compounding impact over a lifetime, resulting in significantly less retirement savings. Women have 65% less 401k savings on average at retirement age and about 20% less to withdraw from their Supplemental Social Security compared to men.
women.section_gender_desc: On average, women earn 84 cents on the dollar relative to men. This gap widens for black and Hispanic women, who earn 70 and 65 cents on the dollar respectively when compared to white men.
women.section_gender_desc_1: On average, employees in female-dominated industries are more likely to earn significantly less than those in male-dominated industries
women.section_gender_desc_2: Research has shown that hiring managers are less likely to hire mothers than women who don’t have kids.
women.section_domestic_desc: Even in today’s social landscape, women bear a disproportionate share of caregiving and other domestic responsibilities, pulling them away from earning at work and slowing their career progression.
women.section_domestic_desc_1: According to a Pew Research Study, women in egalitarian marriages spend more than double the amount of time on housework than their husbands each week (4.6 hours vs. 1.9 hours for men).
women.section_domestic_desc_2: Women take on a majority of childcare responsibilities and are often the first to be turned to when another family member needs care.
women.section_healthcare_desc_1: Healthcare costs for employed women in the United States are estimated to be $15.4 billion greater than those for employed men.23 This financial burden, in combination with the gender wage disparity, negatively impacts female employees and destabilizes their financial and health statuses.
women.section_healthcare_desc_2: The average woman (regardless of age) experiences disproportionately higher out-of-pocket medical expenses. This persists even when we exclude maternity-related services. Nevertheless, 40% of children are born to unmarried women.
women.section_debt_desc_1: Women are more likely than men to hold debt in just about every category, including credit cards, student loans, and car loans. In a recent T. Rowe Price study, 1 in 4 women reported a negative net worth (versus 1 in 10 men).
women.section_debt_desc_2: The widest gap exists with student loan debt — women are nearly 60% more likely than men to have student loan debt, as women tend to take out more in student loans and pay back less due to lower income.
women.section_mindset_desc: It’s easy to assume that gender has no correlation with how people view their finances, but the truth is that women think about and behave with their money very differently from men. Women regard money as a means to enhance the quality of life for both themselves and especially their families, aiming to achieve concrete objectives. Their focus is typically on pressing priorities such as day-to-day expenditures, savings, debt management, and budget upkeep.
women.section_pessimism_desc: Women are more likely to feel pessimistic about their financial situation and financial future. In an Ally survey, participants were asked to select emotions that represent how they feel when thinking about money and the near-term future. Women frequently selected negative emotions, such as worried, overwhelmed, pessimistic, and disappointed; while men frequently selected positive emotions such as motivated, confident, optimistic, and satisfied.
women.section_confidence_gap_desc: Women report lower confidence almost across the board when considering financial activities, including saving for goals, managing household debt, and selecting investment. Interestingly, researchers have found that women are more likely to answer “I don’t know” to these types of questions when the option is available, even if they would otherwise get the answer correct.
women.section_investing_desc: The research shows that women make better investing decisions than men, even though they feel less confident investing their money. Women are less likely to make an investment in a speculative stock, make fewer trades on average than men, and are less likely to sell during an economic downturn, earning them an estimated 1.8% more than men in returns.
women.section_staying_power_desc: Women are slightly less motivated by rates and promotions, and more likely to care about experience and level of service. In a TM Studio survey, fewer women (67% of women vs. 73% of men) indicated that they would sign up for a new bank account if the incentive was appealing enough. Women who have switched banks are more likely to cite a life event, such as a relationship change as the motivation to switch.
women.section_FI: What do women want from financial institutions?
women.section_FI_desc_1: Securing money is tied to being responsible and fulfilling one’s duty to the family. Ultimately, one’s relationship with money can reveal who someone is at their core. While finance has typically been considered a rational space, women need a deep emotional engagement with their finances as an innately personal and private topic representing both safety and success. Many women view their finances as personal and private and appreciate when financial institutions build and establish trust.
women.section_FI_desc_2: These are four key areas where opportunities lie to enhance women's engagement, build trust, and ensure if they feel valued by their financial institutions:
women.section_seen_desc: Women don’t inherently view their gender as their “primary” identity. They relate more to their unique experiences, responsibilities, and roles, so it’s important to have a diverse representation of age, gender, and ethnicity. Women need better communication and engagement to feel like this is “a place for me.” We must include women and make this feel like a place where they belong, matching the customer experience with the brand promise.
women.section_partnership_desc: Women are searching for a deeper relationship with their supportive financial provider who delivers a truly empathic connection.  They prioritize the financial security and safety, as well as great customer service at the forefront of the mind. When banks follow their promises for products and features, women build more trust in their financial institutions.
women.section_convenience_desc: When considering all the systemic barriers and responsibilities women face while shouldering a significantly disproportionate amount of emotional labor at work  and home, it becomes clear why they’re stressed and don’t have enough time to manage everything on their plate. Joe Coughlin recommended to us to “ease the roles, ease the stress - be transparent... she’s got a lot to do, be her ALLY.
women.section_empowerment_desc_1: Confidence and trust are crucial in women's decision-making when choosing their primary financial institutions. Women invest significant time doing research to find the right bank, placing importance on the bank's brand reputation and communication. Women gain confidence by starting small and validating their decisions with their trusted connections, typically including their family and friends.
women.section_empowerment_desc_2: We have an opportunity to elevate women's financial confidence, loyalty and trust by inviting them to have a seat at the table. We need to invite women to join the conversation, understand this is a place for them, and feel empowered to take full control of their financial lives.
women.section_factors: Factors to consider to alleviate her loads:
women.section_factors_desc_1: Don’t make her guess what you mean or leave space for misunderstanding
women.section_factors_desc_2: Make her feel like she's getting more out of the experience faster.
women.section_factors_desc_3: Where is there an opportunity to ease the load of her responsibilities?
women.section_ally_desc: Primarily, we reviewed Ally’s deposits customers and accounts, focusing on the foundational products (particularly spending & saving accounts) that typically drive engagement and deepened relationships. Although I'm not able to disclose company confidential information about customer data, here's the summary of our findings:
women.section_ally_list_1: Ally may have become more appealing to women over the past several years, and they feel supported by the marketing campaigns with an emphasis on women and the community
women.section_ally_list_2: Women banking with Ally actually are more satisfied and more likely to promote and feel more valued than men.
women.section_ally_list_3: Women are more resonated with financial management tools to organize and optimize day-to-day spending and savings than men, as the report shows the highest satisfaction with Ally overall and have the highest Net Promoter Scores (NPS).
women.section_conclusion_desc_1: Women have made immense social and economic progress over the past handful of decades, and evidence indicates that the trend will only strengthen over the coming years. However, the very real disadvantages in their financial journeys are starkly apparent, especially when comparing their finances against men’s at the critical milestone of retirement.
women.section_conclusion_desc_2: We should take this opportunity to acknowledge that what women need from their bank is not what has been traditionally offered to them.
google-en.description_hero: Designed and localized virtual agents for Google Cloud Contact Center to assist global customers with their inquiries.
google-en.section_overview_desc: Originally, the Google Cloud virtual agent was designed to assist customers in American English for the U.S. audience only. As the product expanded globally, it was necessary to localize the virtual agents to support multiple languages and cultures in different countries. This involved not only translating the content, but also adapting the conversation design to ensure it resonated with diverse group of customers.
google-en.section_problem_desc_1: How might we effectively communicate with customers globally and ensure that we're providing the same quality experience to all customers in different languages and cultures?
google-en.section_problem_desc_3: Addition of self-service capabilities to the routing bot.
google-en.section_persona_desc: Sketching rough iterations of each screen on paper ensured that the elements translated to digital wireframes would effectively address the user pain points.
google-en.section_sample_dialogs_desc: I created sample dialogs to visualize the 'happy-path' conversations between the virtual agent and the user. I wanted to ensure that the conversations were natural and the questions were easy to follow.
google-en.section_sample_dialogs_EN_tran: Transliteration from localized Japanese to English
google-en.section_VUIspec_desc: I created a VUI specification document to outline the end-to-end conversation design, while covering all possible edge cases. This document served as a reference for the development team to ensure consistency and quality in the implementation of the virtual agent.
google-en.section_VUIspec_disclaimer: Due to the confidentiality of the project, I'm not able to share the actual VUI specification document. Here's a brief overview of the structure and key elements included in the document.
google-en.section_VUIspec_desc_2: Identify the entry and exit paths
google-en.section_VUIspec_desc_3: Include edge case scenarios such as no-input and no-matching utterances
google-en.section_VUIspec_testing_desc: I worked closely with the development team to conduct QA testing on the virtual agent. This involved testing the conversation flows, ensuring that the virtual agent was able to handle various user inputs and scenarios, and validating that the localized content was accurate and culturally appropriate.
